objective: Extract one supported safe-file-publication backend for pi-artifacts and compatible context reports, preserving canonical paths, bounded content, collision and symlink defenses, atomic exclusive publication, and pi-swe's exclusive ownership of workflow.json.

in: Characterize pi-artifacts normalization, canonical naming, size bounds, collision, traversal, symlink, atomicity, durability, and error behavior.
Identify secure publication overlap in pi-context report output and extract the minimal reusable backend.
Migrate pi-artifacts and typed pi-context Markdown/JSON report operations to the backend without changing paths or bytes.
Centralize the shared adversarial path/publication safety matrix and document ownership boundaries.
Retain pi-swe workflow authority publication as a separate privileged path owned only by SweService/store.
out: Redesigning the artifact tool or changing canonical artifact locations and filenames.
Allowing the shared backend to create or modify any initiative workflow.json.
Migrating unrelated arbitrary file writes or creating a general filesystem framework.
Changing pi-context telemetry semantics beyond its report-publication adapter.

constraints: After initiatives 01-03 establish provider and HUD boundaries, this initiative may proceed in parallel with 04-pi-swe-todo-separation and 06-pi-commands-catalog-ownership; it does not depend on their completion.
Treat the existing pi-swe workflow publication boundary as fixed input: workflow.json remains solely written by pi-swe, regardless of parallel execution.
workflow.json must be explicitly denied by shared publication APIs and remain solely written by pi-swe.
Preserve exclusive no-overwrite behavior, stable parent-relative operations, traversal/symlink defenses, size bounds, file and directory sync, and atomic publication.
Existing artifact and context-report path names and content remain byte-compatible.
Shared backend contains no Pi tool/command registration or domain-specific workflow lifecycle logic.

acceptanceCriteria.text: One minimal backend owns reusable safe artifact/report publication mechanics for pi-artifacts and pi-context.
Artifact tool and context Markdown/JSON report paths, names, content, size bounds, collision, and error behavior remain compatible.
Traversal, symlink, parent-swap, collision, interruption, and concurrent-publication cases fail closed without overwrite or partial publication.
The shared backend cannot create or modify workflow.json, and pi-swe remains its sole publication authority.
Focused security and full repository qualification passes with independent review.

assessment.reason: The extension is well-designed, but extracting security-sensitive publication code across consumers risks path traversal, symlink races, overwrite, durability, and workflow authority violations.
unknowns: The exact overlap worth sharing must be confirmed against current implementations.
Platform support differences for stable directory descriptors may constrain the reusable API.

practices.reason: Existing security and byte/path behavior must be captured before centralization.
The shared backend should expose only safe artifact/report publication and explicitly deny workflow authority paths.
Multiple consumers and privileged workflow boundaries require full negative testing and independent review.

obligations.text: Characterize artifact and context-report bytes/paths plus traversal, symlink, parent-swap, collision, interruption, concurrency, size, durability, and workflow.json denial cases before extraction.
Verify the shared backend has no registration or workflow lifecycle dependencies, publishes exclusively and atomically, preserves consumer outputs, and rejects workflow.json and unsafe paths.
Run artifact, context, SWE security, typecheck, dependency, command, performance, and full repository gates, then obtain independent security and boundary review.

work.title: Characterize artifact and report publication security

testing.approach: Extend golden and adversarial fixtures before moving any publication primitive.
testing.reason: Safe extraction requires a proven behavioral and security baseline.

work.title: Extract and adopt the safe publication backend

testing.approach: Implement a least-capability backend, migrate pi-artifacts and context reports, and rerun consumer and adversarial tests.
testing.reason: Centralization is valuable only if it reduces duplication without broadening write authority.

work.title: Document ownership and qualify publication safety

testing.approach: Run integrated gates, inspect workflow authority denial and public compatibility, and obtain independent source-bound review.
testing.reason: Security-sensitive shared code requires repository-wide evidence and distinct review.

decisions.text: Share artifact/report publication mechanics but not pi-swe workflow authority publication.
decisions.basis: workflow.json has stronger lifecycle and identity invariants and must remain exclusively owned by pi-swe.
The review identifies it as the best-designed extension and recommends only optional utility extraction.

decisions.text: Run this work in the same post-provider wave as initiatives 04 and 06 when capacity permits.
decisions.basis: The consolidation plan identifies UI, publication, and scaffolding migrations as separate regression surfaces that need not block one another.

risks.text: Generalization weakens path or race defenses.
risks.mitigation: Use a shared adversarial matrix and a minimal capability-oriented API.

risks.text: Context reports change names or bytes.
risks.mitigation: Retain golden path/content fixtures for Markdown and JSON outputs.

risks.text: The backend becomes a route around SweService.
risks.mitigation: Explicitly deny workflow.json and independently review write-authority boundaries.
